caption: The drawing contains three black line illustrations of an easy chair, each presenting a different view: the top view (upper left), the front view (lower left), and the side view (lower right). The armchair depicted has curved arms, a tall backrest, upholstered seat, and ornate cabriole front legs with animal claw feet. The drawing includes red measurement lines and numerical annotations indicating various dimensions in inches, with a scale at the bottom showing 1/10 inch representing 1 inch. The top view shows the chair's seat and arm layout, while the front view reveals the full height, leg, and seat proportions. The side view details the profile of the chair, showing the seat's depth and the back’s angle. To the right of the top view, there is a handwritten label with information about the object described, including its material (mahogany), approximate date (1760–1770), acquisition information, room and catalog numbers, location (Metropolitan Museum of Art), and the name of the drafter (M. Rosenshield-Von Paulin). The text and dimensions are rendered in black and red ink respectively, on a light beige background.
title: Wing Chair
